title: Family Days Out on a Budget: 15 Ways to Spend Less
description: Fifteen ways to enjoy family days out on a budget: free attractions, rail 2FOR1, kids-go-free rules, picnics, off-peak dates and passes.
h1: Family days out on a budget: 15 ways to spend less
intro: A brilliant day out doesn’t need a big budget. These are Scout’s favourite money-saving habits, all simple and all real.

image.alt: A family relaxing on a picnic blanket in a park

cardText: Fifteen simple, real ways to spend less on family days out.

blocks.title: Scout’s top three
blocks.text: If you only do three things: book online ahead, pack a picnic and check who goes free. Those alone can save a family a lot on a big day out.

sections.html:
1. Book online: gate prices are usually the highest.
  2. Go off-peak: term-time weekdays cost less at date-priced attractions.
  3. Check who goes free: under-3s and under-5s often do. See kids go free.
  4. Use the train for 2FOR1: see how it works.
  5. Get a railcard for family train travel.
  6. Compare passes if you’ll go back: annual pass vs day tickets.
  7. Use rewards: supermarket points and discount apps.

1. Pack a picnic and refillable bottles: checklist here.
  2. Set a souvenir budget before you arrive.
  3. Skip the photo packages unless they’re really wanted.
  4. Park smart: compare parking with park-and-ride or public transport.
  5. Bring your own buggy and rain gear instead of hiring or buying.

1. Free museums: see free days out.
  2. Beaches, forests and parks with a picnic.
  3. Free events: heritage open days, library activities and local festivals.

faqs.q: How can I make a family day out cheaper?
faqs.a: Book online in advance, go off-peak, check kids-go-free rules, use rail 2FOR1 offers, take a picnic and set a souvenir budget.
